Bessie Love: Early Career and Iconic Portraits from the 1910s Silent Film Era
item.description: Bessie Love, born Juanita Horton on September 10, 1898, was an American-British actress who became prominent in silent and early sound films during the 1910s. Known for her diminutive stature, expressive eyes, and naturalistic acting style, Love's career began in 1915 after she was discovered by legendary director D.W. Griffith. Griffith renamed her Bessie Love and recognized her potential, nicknaming her 'Our Mary' due to her innocent and emotive screen presence similar to Mary Pickford. She was cast in significant early roles, including small parts in 'The Birth of a Nation' (1915) and as the Bride of Cana in 'Intolerance' (1916). Under Griffith's Triangle Fine Arts company, she co-starred with notable silent film stars such as Douglas Fairbanks and William S. Hart. By 1916-1917, she was headlining feature melodramas like 'A Sister of Six' and 'Nina, the Flower Girl.' item.title: House Foreign Affairs Committee to Hold Hearing on Foreign Influence Operations in U.S. Nonprofits
item.description: The House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia has scheduled an open hearing titled 'Trojan Horses: Covert Foreign Malign Influence Operations in America' to examine how foreign governments and organizations may be using nonprofits and activist networks as 'Trojan horses' to influence U.S. politics, public opinion, and strategic policy. The hearing, set for Tuesday, will focus on influence operations from China, Cuba, and Iran, as well as pro-Palestinian groups. The committee aims to investigate whether America's open political system and nonprofit sector are being exploited by foreign governments seeking to infiltrate and influence American society from within. The hearing expands on previous congressional scrutiny of foreign influence, particularly regarding the Singham network, which has been linked to Chinese Communist Party-aligned organizations. item.title: Texas Couple's H-E-B Engagement Photos Capture Hearts Across Texas
item.description: A Texas couple, Cara DeGaish and David Quiroz, has gained attention for their engagement photos taken at an H-E-B grocery store in Houston. The photos, posted on Instagram by DeGaish on September 3, 2026, quickly garnered over 3,000 likes and numerous comments. The couple chose the H-E-B location on Bunker Hill Road in Houston, which holds significant meaning for them. David Quiroz worked as an assistant store manager at H-E-B during his college years, while Cara DeGaish grew up near an H-E-B in Portland, Texas, across the Nueces Bay Causeway from Corpus Christi. The couple met as musical theater majors at Sam Houston State University in Huntsville, where they initially had a rocky start but eventually developed a strong friendship through their shared love for H-E-B. They often visited the store for casual walks, to rank seasonal chips, or to grab snacks from the bulk aisle. After becoming engaged in December 2025, DeGaish approached photographer Miranda Zaebst, who also works at Hous

item.title: Texas AG Ken Paxton Faces Backlash for Highlighting Women's Job Growth Amid Conservative Tensions
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a Republican Senate candidate, has sparked controversy within conservative circles by promoting the August job growth statistics that show women have gained 765,000 jobs since December 2024, while men lost approximately 6,000 positions. Paxton's post on X, which echoed the White House's celebration of women's employment gains, drew sharp criticism from within the conservative movement. Megan Basham of The Daily Wire called it 'tone deaf' and criticized the Republican establishment for failing to understand the current moment. Historian Rebecca Jo Plant noted that the backlash was 'sad but predictable,' emphasizing that men's economic struggles are not caused by women's employment but by wealth concentration. The article highlights growing tensions within the conservative movement over family policy, as Republicans attempt to balance economic data with policies encouraging women to leave the workforce. item.title: Rare Still Photographs Capture United Airlines Flight 175 Approaching World Trade Center South Tower on 9/11
item.description: On the morning of September 11, 2001, United Airlines Flight 175, a Boeing 767 bound for Los Angeles from Boston's Logan International Airport, was hijacked by al-Qaeda terrorists. Approximately 17 minutes after American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower of the World Trade Center, Flight 175 was deliberately flown into the South Tower between the 77th and 85th floors at 9:03 a.m. EDT. The impact caused a massive explosion and fire, resulting in the deaths of all 65 people on board and hundreds more inside the building. The collision severely damaged the South Tower's structural integrity, leading to its collapse 56 minutes later at 9:59 a.m. While most imagery of the event comes from video footage captured by news crews and amateur videographers who were already filming after the North Tower attack, still photographs of Flight 175 in flight are exceptionally rare. item.title: China and US Compete for AI Influence in Middle East Amid Environmental Concerns
item.description:
The article discusses the intensifying competition between China and the United States for influence in the Middle East, particularly in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). China's President Xi Jinping recently made his first state visit to Egypt since 2016, deepening economic and security ties between Beijing and Cairo. During this visit, China and Egypt agreed to launch the third phase of a cooperative industrial zone in the Suez Canal, as Egypt seeks to diversify its foreign policy relations beyond just the United States. The US remains Egypt's major security partner, providing $1.3 billion in military aid annually, but faces growing geopolitical competition from China.
The article highlights that Middle Eastern countries, particularly those in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), are facing significant environmental challenges as they develop AI infrastructure. item.title: BBC Expert Proposes Breathing Technique as Non-Medication Aid for COPD Patients
item.description: A recent study has revealed a non-medication breathing technique that could significantly benefit the approximately 1.4 million people in the UK suffering from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Dr. Oscar Duke, a BBC health expert, discussed this technique on BBC Morning Live, emphasizing its potential to improve quality of life for COPD patients without relying solely on medication. COPD, which affects about 2% of the UK population and 4.5% of those over 40, is the second most common lung disease after asthma, causing difficulty in exhaling due to narrowed airways and damaged lung tissue. It encompasses conditions like chronic bronchitis and emphysema, often linked to smoking but with various other causes. Current treatments typically involve inhalers and pulmonary rehabilitation, which includes exercise and education. However, the study highlighted an additional approach: pursed-lip breathing, where individuals inhale through the nose and exhale slowly through pursed lips,

item.title: Artist Develops Tool to Improve Representation of Natural Black Hair in Video Games
item.description: The article discusses the prevalence of 'Killmonger locs'—a stiff, short-dreaded hairstyle inspired by Michael B. Jordan's character in Black Panther—as a default for Black video game characters. Danielle Udogaranya, a technical artist known as Ebonix, has created a Blender plugin called the Loc & Kinky Strand Generator Tool to address this issue. The tool allows creators to generate natural Black hairstyles more efficiently, reducing the time and effort required to code these styles. Udogaranya explains that natural Black hairstyles have been historically underrepresented in video games due to technical limitations, with developers often defaulting to the 'Killmonger locs' because they are easier to code. She notes that while some progress has been made, such as the Code My Crown initiative by Dove and the Open Source Afro Hair Library, and EA's recent free downloadable content for The Sims 4, the industry still faces significant challenges. item.title: Houthi forces advance toward key oil chokepoint in Yemen, threatening global trade routes
item.description: The United States is facing a potential strategic disaster as Yemen's Houthi rebels advance toward capturing Mocha, a coastal town in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical chokepoint for global shipping. According to The Guardian, this development could open a second front in President Donald Trump's war against Iran, which has been widely criticized as deeply unpopular. The Bab el-Mandeb Strait, along with the Strait of Hormuz, accounts for approximately a quarter of daily petroleum and crude shipments and nearly one-third of the world's maritime trade. The Houthis have previously vowed to block all Saudi Arabian shipments through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and their recent capture of Mocha marks a significant step toward controlling Yemen's west coast on the Red Sea. This strategic shift would bring Iran and its proxies closer to full control of two major shipping chokepoints on opposite sides of the Arabian Peninsula. item.title: Trump Proposes $5,000 Payments to Americans if Republicans Control Congress
item.description: President Donald Trump has announced a proposal to provide $5,000 payments to every American adult, contingent upon Republicans maintaining control of Congress in the upcoming November midterm elections. The announcement, made during a speech at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, has sparked inquiries regarding the feasibility, legality, and funding sources of the proposed benefit. Trump has previously pledged similar direct payments since returning to office, but this latest proposal has drawn particular attention due to its scale and timing. The Washington Post article, authored by Aoife Walsh and Victoria Craw, details the president's commitment to this financial incentive, emphasizing its role as a political strategy to secure Republican dominance in Congress. The article notes that the proposal is part of a broader campaign to rally support among voters, particularly those who may be concerned about economic conditions. item.title: Congresswoman Conducts Surprise Visit to ICE Facility Amid Reports of Medical Neglect and Overcrowding
item.description: U.S. Representative Yassamin Ansari, a Democrat from Phoenix, conducted a surprise oversight visit to a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Phoenix on Wednesday, September 10, 2026, following reports by the Arizona Mirror that detainees were staying longer and in larger numbers than in previous years. The facility, located in a midtown Phoenix office building housing the Arizona headquarters for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and ICE, has been the subject of weekly protests since last summer, some of which led to clashes between protesters and ICE officers. The Phoenix ICE District Office, which serves as the primary base of operations for ICE in Arizona, also houses a temporary hold facility with 10 holding cells capable of accommodating up to 150 people. However, the facility lacks beds, on-site medical services, limited access to food, and no accessible showers for detainees. item.title: Genetic Study Identifies Repeat Expansions in NOTCH2NLC and RFC1 Genes as Cause of Unexplained Inherited Neuropathies
item.description: A recent study published in the Journal of Human Genetics has identified that non-coding repeat expansions within the NOTCH2NLC and RFC1 genes contribute to unsolved inherited peripheral neuropathies. The research team, led by Xin-Yun Zhang and colleagues from Zhejiang University School of Medicine, examined patients with unexplained peripheral neuropathies and found that specific genetic mutations in these genes were responsible for the condition. The study involved 100 patients with inherited peripheral neuropathies who had not been diagnosed through standard genetic testing. Through advanced genomic analysis, the researchers discovered that 15% of these patients had non-coding repeat expansions in the NOTCH2NLC gene, while 8% had similar expansions in the RFC1 gene. These genetic mutations lead to the production of toxic polyglycine proteins that disrupt cellular functions, particularly in nerve cells. The findings are significant because they provide a genetic explanation for a sub

item.title: Rice University Advances Dark Matter Search with Levitated Magnet Experiment
item.description: Rice University physicists have made significant progress in the search for ultraheavy dark matter using a novel experimental approach. The team employed a grain-of-sand-sized magnet levitated above a superconductor cooled to near absolute zero temperatures. This innovative setup allowed them to probe dark matter particles approximately 10 million times heavier than those examined in previous levitated-particle experiments. The research, presented at a particle-physics and cosmology conference in September 2026, did not detect any dark matter signals but established new limits on the mass range of potential dark matter candidates. The POLONAISE experiment, which uses a permanent magnet weighing 0.356 milligrams held in a superconducting tantalum trap, represents a seven-order-of-magnitude extension in the mass reach of levitated sensors. The researchers monitored the system for 219.66 hours (about 9.15 days) during overnight periods to minimize external disturbances. While eight candid

item.title: Beijing Haichang Ocean Park to Open in 2027 as World's Largest New Aquarium Under Construction
item.description: Beijing Haichang Ocean Park, a RMB4.2 billion (US$625 million, £462 million) marine attraction currently under construction next to Universal Beijing Resort, is targeting a 2027 opening. The project, designed by Legacy Entertainment, covers 157,100 square meters (1.7 million square feet) in Beijing's Tongzhou district. Legacy Entertainment states it will be the world's largest new aquarium facility currently under construction, with an expected annual visitor count of four million. The primarily indoor attraction combines a next-generation aquarium with an eight-storey resort hotel. The complex will rise to 23.9 meters, featuring three above-ground exhibit levels and two subterranean floors for parking and services. Haichang describes the development as a 'fifth-generation aquarium,' integrating ecology, science education, research, interactive experiences, exhibitions, art, and a themed hotel. item.title: Wisconsin Gubernatorial Debate Cancelled After Both Candidates Declined Participation
item.description: The Wisconsin Broadcasters Association Foundation has canceled its planned gubernatorial candidate debate for October, marking the end of a 36-year tradition. The organization had initially announced in April that it would host a debate between the Republican and Democratic nominees for governor, a practice it had maintained since 1990. Both Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, the Democratic candidate, and U.S. Representative Tom Tiffany, the Republican candidate, were invited to participate. However, the debate was canceled because neither candidate accepted the invitation. Tiffany stated he was only willing to participate in one debate, claiming it was 'sufficient' for the race. The foundation explained that, based on legal precedent, multiple candidates must accept invitations for a debate to be aired. Both invitations were sent, but neither was accepted. item.title: Conservative Podcaster Katie Miller Faces FTC Disclosure Allegations Over AI Chatbot Criticisms
item.description: Conservative podcaster Katie Miller has been accused of potentially violating federal disclosure laws after a Washington Post analysis revealed she criticized AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Google's Gemini over nine months without disclosing her financial stake in a competing company. The Post found Miller published nearly 500 posts criticizing these chatbots, accusing them of liberal bias, endangering children, and lacking security, while simultaneously promoting Elon Musk's xAI's Grok chatbot over 160 times. A recent financial filing disclosed that Miller holds more than $1 million in xAI stock, purchased in December after she began consulting for the company. Legal experts, including Harvard Law School professor Rebecca Tushnet, stated that Federal Trade Commission guidelines require disclosure of financial relationships when promoting or attacking competing products. item.title: Clearview AI Develops Prototype AI Tool to Assist Law Enforcement in Online Data Aggregation
item.description: Clearview AI, a face recognition company known for scraping over 3 billion internet photos in 2020, is developing a prototype AI tool called InquiryIQ. This experimental system, currently not available to customers, aims to help law enforcement automatically gather information about individuals identified through facial recognition searches. InquiryIQ would analyze web sources to build profiles containing possible employers, aliases, associates, social media accounts, addresses, and other personal details. The tool uses AI models, including those from xAI (Elon Musk's company), to perform web searches and analyze images. Clearview emphasizes that human analysts would still review and verify all findings before they are added to a case file. The company states InquiryIQ is a prototype for internal testing only, not a product ready for release. Experts warn that while such tools could speed up investigations, they also lower the cost of surveillance, potentially enabling more widespread

item.title: Ohio Lawmakers Push to Block Flock Cameras Amid Privacy Concerns
item.description: Ohio lawmakers are leading a bipartisan effort to restrict the use of Flock cameras, which are automated license plate readers operated by a private company. The lawmakers, including Reps. Tristan Rader, Levi Dean, Darnell Brewer, and Justin Pizzulli, have urged the state’s Director of Transportation to halt new permits for these cameras and review existing ones. They argue that public roads should not be used to create a statewide surveillance network without proper oversight. The letter emphasizes that while the cameras can aid in solving crimes, the widespread tracking of innocent citizens without warrants or individualized suspicion is problematic. The debate has intensified in Ohio’s political landscape, with both major party candidates for governor addressing the issue. Democrat Amy Acton initially supported the cameras but has since called for 'strict guardrails' and pledged to ban Flock cameras if elected. item.title: Trump Shifts Focus from Vance to Rubio as Potential 2028 Successor, Insider Reports
item.description: According to a report by Politico, President Donald Trump is privately changing his tone regarding his preferred successor for the 2028 presidential election, shifting from Vice President JD Vance to Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The report, based on two inside sources, indicates that Trump has scaled back his focus on polling between Vance and Rubio, and has begun speaking more positively about Vance in recent months. This shift comes after earlier indications in March that Trump was leaning toward Rubio, with some Republicans noting his 'body language' suggesting as much. The White House insider had previously reported that Trump's body language indicated a preference for Rubio, while Vice President Vance had reportedly been at odds with the president over his decision to attack Iran and had performed poorly in hypothetical 2028 matchups with leading Democratic candidates. item.title: Trump Reiterates Misleading Claim About 'Dumb' Spelling at Midterm Convention
item.description:
President Donald Trump faced widespread mockery and criticism at the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas, on September 9, 2026, for repeating his claim that most people do not know the word 'dumb' ends with a 'B.' The 80-year-old president, who has been promoting this assertion for months, told the cheering crowd that he had recently discovered the spelling of the word, stating, 'You take out the E and you replace it with a U, and nobody knows that 'dumb' has a B at the end of it. Most people think it's D-U-M, and that's fine. So we take out the E, replace it with a U, and they're 'Dumocrats' because their policies are so bad.'
Trump's claim, which has been widely debunked, drew immediate reactions from critics and social media users. Representative Malcolm Kenyatta (D-PA) sarcastically remarked, 'You really put the B in dumb sir,' while popular X account Spiro's Ghost commented, 'OMG his demented, dementia eaten brain said this AGAIN.' item.title: Diatomaceous Earth Faucet Mat Gains Popularity for Its Absorbent Properties
item.description: The article discusses a diatomaceous earth splash guard that has become popular for its absorbent properties. The product, which wraps around the base of a faucet, is designed to contain water splashes and prevent messes in the kitchen. According to the article, the mat is made from diatomaceous earth, a natural material created from fossilized algae, which has a porous structure that absorbs moisture quickly. The porous nature of the material allows it to disperse water over a larger area, facilitating faster evaporation compared to traditional fabric mats. The article cites several consumer reviews praising the product, with one reviewer calling it 'FUCKING WIZARDRY' and another describing it as a 'total game-changer.' The mat is available in three gray tones and various sizes to fit different sink lengths. It is also noted that the mat cannot be cut or altered to fit additional knobs beyond the faucet. item.title: Lawrence O’Donnell Warns Trump's Midterm Convention May Be His Final Political Appearance
item.description: Lawrence O'Donnell, host of MS NOW, has commented on President Donald Trump's recent appearance at the Republican National Committee's 'Trump-a-Palooza' convention in Dallas, Texas. O'Donnell suggested that Trump's speech at this 'midterm convention' could potentially be his last political convention appearance, stating that Trump's 'self-worshipping' convention is a sign of his political vulnerability ahead of the midterms. The president's appearance came amid his unpopular war with Iran, which has driven up gas prices and damaged his approval ratings. Trump promised voters $5,000 checks if Republicans maintain control of Congress, a pledge he has made before but failed to deliver on. O'Donnell pointed out that Trump made a similar promise in September 2024, which was not fulfilled, and noted that gas prices in Alaska were $5.03 per gallon, $0.81 above the national average, as evidence that Trump's promises are unreliable. item.title: Mike Johnson Faces Accusations of Misrepresentation After Claiming Full Attendance at GOP Convention Amid Empty Seating
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) faced significant criticism and accusations of misleading the public after making a claim during a Newsmax interview that the Republican midterm convention in Dallas was completely full, despite visible empty seats in the venue. The incident occurred on Wednesday evening as the Republican National Committee (RNC) held its first-ever midterm convention at the American Airlines Center, headlined by President Donald Trump. During the interview with Newsmax host Rob Finnerty, Johnson stated that every seat was full, including the upper deck, and that there was a long line of people waiting to enter. However, the broadcast footage showed numerous empty seats in the upper deck and gaps in the lower bowl, contradicting Johnson's statement. Clips of the exchange quickly spread on social media, with independent journalist Aaron Rupar noting that the camera panned to show 'gobs of empty seats' while Johnson made his claim. item.title: Trump's 9/11 Claims Contradicted by Historical Records and Fact-Checkers
item.description: The article critically examines former President Donald Trump's repeated false claims about his involvement in the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks. It details how Trump has consistently fabricated stories about being at Ground Zero, personally leading rescue efforts, and risking his life during the attacks, despite no evidence supporting these assertions. The piece references Trump's 2026 interview on the 25th anniversary of 9/11, where he claimed to have sent hundreds of workers to assist in rescue operations, while simultaneously receiving $150,000 from a federal fund meant to aid businesses in Lower Manhattan affected by the attacks. The article notes that Trump's 40 Wall Street property was not damaged in the attacks, contradicting his earlier statements. It also highlights that Trump's claims about his 9/11 involvement have evolved over time, including a 2021 story about hearing a building creak and being saved by firefighters, which fact-checkers found to be entirely fabrica

item.title: New Analysis Challenges Dark Energy Theory, Suggesting Cosmic Expansion May Be Slowing
item.description: A recent study analyzing over 1,700 supernovae has raised questions about whether the universe's expansion is truly accelerating. Researchers from the University of Oxford, after accounting for the ages of the stars that produce these supernovae, found evidence suggesting that cosmic expansion might actually be slowing down. The study, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, also notes that the apparent acceleration of the universe appears to vary with direction, which would be difficult to explain if dark energy were the driving force behind cosmic expansion. This finding has sparked debate within the cosmological community, with some researchers, including Professor Maria Vincenzi from Oxford, arguing that current observations continue to support an accelerating universe. The study's conclusions set the stage for major tests by upcoming astronomical observatories, which will provide more precise data to resolve this ongoing scientific dispute. The research cha

item.title: Keshet International's 'The Escape' Stars Yehuda Levi in Cross-Border Thriller Set in Colombian Jungle
item.description: Keshet International has announced that Yehuda Levi, known for his role in 'A Body that Works,' will star in the upcoming eight-episode international cross-border action-thriller 'The Escape' (Hebrew title: 'Ha'Bricha'). Set deep in the Colombian jungle, the series follows the son of a religious cult leader who escapes but must leave his wife and child behind. He teams up with ex-Mossad operative Carmeli (Levi) to rescue his family, only to discover the cult has an alliance with a drug cartel, escalating the conflict into a full-scale war. The cast includes Ido Tako as Yoel, Naya Bienstock as Feigy, Roy Shachar Kremerman as Nachman, and Mark Ivanir as the cult leader. Created and written by Ariel Cohen, the series is directed by Yoav and Doron Paz, who also co-created 'The Golem.' Filmed across Colombia, Georgia, and Israel, 'The Escape' will premiere on Keshet 12 in Israel later this year, with global distribution handled by Keshet International. item.title: Rhode Island Governor Dan McKee Loses Democratic Primary to Former CVS Executive Helena Foulkes
item.description: In a significant political development, Rhode Island Governor Dan McKee has lost his bid for renomination in the Democratic primary to former CVS executive Helena Foulkes. This marks the first time since 2018 that a sitting governor has been defeated in a primary challenge. McKee, who is 75 years old, had been the governor since 2021, following the resignation of Gina Raimondo to join President Joe Biden's Cabinet. Polling data indicates that McKee was one of the least popular governors in the country. In the 2022 primary, McKee narrowly defeated Foulkes, who is 62 years old. The primary results were reported on September 10, 2026, at 3:49 a.m. EDT, with McKee's defeat being a notable outcome in the political landscape of Rhode Island. The Washington Post, which reported on the event, highlighted the historical significance of McKee becoming the first governor to lose renomination since 2018. The article also included a photo of McKee and Foulkes, with images provided by Mark Stockwell

item.title: CNN Host Questions Feasibility of Trump's $5,000 Dividend Promise for Midterm Voters
item.description: President Donald Trump announced at the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas, on September 9, 2026, that he would issue $5,000 dividend checks to each adult American citizen if Republicans maintain their congressional majorities in the upcoming midterm elections. CNN's Audie Cornish questioned the feasibility of this pledge during 'CNN This Morning,' highlighting a potential issue with the funding source. Cornish noted that following a recent Supreme Court ruling, tariff revenue had to be refunded to companies, and many companies did not pass these refunds on to consumers. She expressed uncertainty about where the revenue for such a large payout would come from, given that the previous pool of tariff revenue was significantly depleted due to legal reasons. Former Biden White House staffer Meghan Hays also criticized the promise, stating that it was easy for Trump to make such pledges without having to fulfill them, as he is unlikely to win the upcoming elections. item.title: Morning Joe Panel Prays for Tim Scott Following Controversial GOP Convention Remarks
item.description: The Morning Joe show, hosted by Joe Scarborough and Mika Brzezinski, held a prayer circle on Thursday morning following a speech by U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) at the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas. The panelists expressed confusion and concern over Scott's remarks, which included him shouting at the audience that Democrats want to 'rip that heart out of our chest.' Scarborough described the speech as 'really weird,' while Brzezinski responded with 'Whoa.' The panelists speculated that Scott might need medical intervention or divine help, prompting Rev. Al Sharpton to suggest a prayer circle. Sharpton urged the group to 'join hands and pray' and specifically asked, 'He's out there — bring him back in, Lord.' The panel also discussed Scott's perceived need to 'kiss the ring' of President Donald Trump, with Sharpton suggesting that Scott's rhetoric was extreme and possibly indicative of mental distress. item.title: Nearly 250,000 Australian Homes Face Threat from Rising Sea Levels, Report Reveals
item.description: A recent report has identified that nearly 250,000 homes across Australia are at risk due to rising sea levels. The findings, published on September 10, 2026, highlight the growing environmental challenge posed by climate change. The report emphasizes the urgent need for coastal communities to implement adaptive measures to protect residential properties from potential flooding and erosion. While the exact locations of the affected homes are not specified in the provided text, the data underscores a significant threat to Australia's coastal infrastructure. The report's release coincides with increasing global awareness of climate-related risks, particularly in regions vulnerable to sea-level rise. Authorities are urged to prioritize long-term planning and investment in coastal defenses to mitigate the escalating risks. item.title: Netflix's 'Crew Girl' Struggles to Balance Representation and Clichés in Rowing Drama
item.description: Netflix's latest young adult series 'Crew Girl' follows 16-year-old Teagan Tao, a single sculler whose life is upended when her father, a wealthy hotelier, is caught stealing money from clients and flees before the FBI can arrest him. Forced to leave their affluent Los Angeles community for Ella's hometown in Massachusetts, Teagan and her mother must navigate a new life at Easton Prep, where she discovers the school's rowing team is exclusively for boys. Determined to join, Teagan becomes the coxswain of the eight-man crew, facing challenges from the team's initial resistance and the need to build camaraderie among the male athletes. The series, created by Vivian Lin, features Miku Martineau as Teagan, Jessica Paré as her mother Ella, and a diverse cast including Sam Braun, Kyle Clark, and Jude Wilson. item.title: Missing 'L' in Republican Convention Sign Sparks Online Mockery
item.description: The Republican National Convention, dubbed 'Trumpalooza' due to its focus on Donald Trump, faced immediate online ridicule after a missing letter 'L' was discovered on a sign at the event's opening in Dallas. The sign, which read 'Da las' instead of 'Dallas,' became a focal point for jokes on social media platforms like X (formerly Twitter). The error, which appeared just minutes after the convention began, was quickly noted by attendees and commentators, with some suggesting it was a deliberate attempt to highlight the event's shortcomings. The missing 'L' was later corrected, but the incident sparked a wave of sarcastic and critical remarks from political observers and the public. Many social media users pointed out the irony of the error, with some humorously suggesting that the Republicans had 'taken the L' early in the convention. The incident reflects the high stakes and intense scrutiny surrounding the midterms, as well as the role of social media in amplifying political comment

item.title: CNN Fact-Checker Disputes Trump's Claims on Inflation and Promises at Midterm Rally
item.description: CNN's Daniel Dale, a senior fact-checker, addressed several claims made by President Donald Trump during his two-hour speech at the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas, on September 9, 2026. Trump asserted that 'we got eggs down lower than during my administration, and food prices, and almost every other item, are rapidly going down.' Dale confirmed that the egg price claim was accurate but refuted the broader statement about declining prices, calling it 'absolutely false' and a 'very important lie.' According to Consumer Price Index data, the recent inflation rate stands at 3.4 percent, with more products becoming more expensive rather than cheaper. Food prices have risen 4.3 percent and grocery prices 3.4 percent since Trump took office, both still climbing. Curated by LensCulture, the show emphasizes narrative restitution, amplifying voices from the past to envision a polyphonic future. Themes of memory, identity, and collective healing are central, with pieces like 'Picnic' and 'Night Riders' interrogating colonial legacies. The exhibition underscores the importance of diverse perspectives in redefining historical narratives, offering a kaleidoscopic vision of cultural resilience. By engaging with both personal and collective histories, the artworks invite viewers to reconsider the power of art in shaping historical memory and fostering reconciliation.

item.title: China's August Imports Fall Short of Estimates as Exports Rise
item.description: China's August trade data revealed mixed results, with imports missing expectations while exports showed growth. According to the report, imports rose 28.2% year-over-year, falling short of the 30% forecast. Exports, however, increased by 25%, driven by strong demand for manufactured goods. The trade surplus widened to $58 billion, reflecting robust export performance. Analysts noted that the data highlights China's ongoing efforts to balance trade flows, with the government emphasizing the need to reduce reliance on foreign markets. The Federal Reserve's monetary policy and the yuan's appreciation were also mentioned as factors influencing trade dynamics. The report also cited comments from G20 officials regarding the importance of trade diversification. Despite the positive export growth, the import shortfall raised questions about domestic demand and potential supply chain adjustments. Overall, the data underscores China's complex trade landscape amid global economic uncertainties.

The ad's exaggerated promises were presented as a satirical take on Trump's public persona. Fallon's segment highlighted the absurdity of Trump's public image while offering a lighthearted commentary on media and political satire. The piece was part of HuffPost Entertainment's coverage of pop culture and political humor, blending real-world events with fictionalized scenarios to critique public figures. item.title: Trump pushes for Bombardier plane ban amid trade tensions with Canada
item.description: President Donald Trump has called for a ban on Bombardier planes in the United States, escalating trade tensions with Canada. The move has drawn criticism from Republican Senator Jerry Moran of Kansas, whose state hosts Bombardier's U.S. headquarters. Trump's comments come amid a trade war with Canada, which has imposed retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods. Bombardier has defended its investments in the U.S., highlighting its role in creating thousands of jobs and its reliance on American supply chains. The dispute underscores growing friction between the U.S. and Canada over trade policies, with Trump emphasizing the need for Canadian companies to operate within the U.S. market. Moran has urged the Trump administration to recognize Bombardier's economic contributions to Kansas and its broader impact on the aerospace industry. The conflict reflects broader challenges in U.S.-Canada trade relations, as both nations navigate a complex web of tariffs and economic pressures.

item.title: Historical Photos Reveal the Daily Struggles of Segregation in Jim Crow America
item.description: This article presents a collection of rare historical photographs documenting the pervasive impact of Jim Crow laws in the United States during the 20th century. Through images of segregated public spaces, civil rights protests, and everyday life under racial discrimination, the collection illustrates the systemic racism that shaped American society. The photographs capture moments from the 1930s to the 1960s, including scenes of segregated streetcars, 'colored' water coolers, and the 1963 March on Washington. The images serve as a visual record of the struggle for civil rights, highlighting both the resilience of activists and the enduring legacy of racial segregation. The collection includes iconic moments such as Governor George Wallace's defiance at the University of Alabama and the aftermath of Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination. These photographs provide a powerful testament to the historical context of racial inequality and the ongoing fight for justice in America.

The device, equipped with artificial intelligence and advanced food preparation systems, can replicate gourmet recipes with precision. Industry experts predict this innovation could redefine restaurant operations and home cooking. The robot's ability to analyze ingredients and adjust cooking times in real-time has attracted attention from chefs and food technologists. While some argue it may reduce human involvement in cooking, proponents highlight its potential to enhance efficiency and consistency in high-volume kitchens. The product is expected to launch in major markets by early 2024, marking a significant milestone in food technology.

This victory opens the door for Shaheen to face Anthony DiLorenzo, a Trump-endorsed Republican, in the November general election. The race is significant as it reflects the broader political dynamics in New Hampshire, where Democrats and Republicans are competing to flip the seat. item.title: Sensex and Nifty Drop Amid West Asia Tensions
item.description: Indian benchmark indices, the Sensex and Nifty, experienced sharp declines in early trading on Wednesday due to escalating tensions in West Asia, which pushed crude oil prices near USD 100 per barrel. IT stocks and fresh foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows further pressured market sentiment. The 30-share BSE Sensex fell 500.25 points to 75,060.61, while the 50-share NSE Nifty dropped 129.40 points to 23,506.10. Analysts warned that sustained high oil prices could intensify inflationary pressures, weaken the rupee, and impact corporate margins. Brent crude prices rose 1.44% to USD 99.33 per barrel, with fears of further disruptions to global energy supplies. Asian markets showed mixed reactions, with South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei 225 rising, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell. Foreign investors sold equities worth Rs 123.19 crore on Tuesday, exacerbating market volatility. The situation highlights the ongoing geopolitical risks affecting global financial markets.

Las denuncias abarcan acusaciones de falta de transparencia en la recopilación de datos, falta de consentimiento explícito para el uso de información sensible y posibles violaciones de normativas de protección de datos. Las empresas han respondido que están cooperando con las autoridades y que han implementado medidas para mejorar la seguridad y privacidad de los usuarios. During a Steele Across America event at the White House, Trump expressed frustration that Crowther, known as 'the man in the red bandana,' had gained more fame than himself. Crowther, a volunteer firefighter, was among the first to rescue survivors from the South Tower after United Airlines Flight 175 struck. His actions, which saved 18 people, were later documented in a 2002 New York Times article and memorialized on the 9/11 Memorial website. Trump posthumously awarded Crowther the Presidential Medal of Freedom during the ceremony. Critics condemned his comments as disrespectful, with many arguing that Crowther's sacrifice should not be diminished by political remarks. item.description: In a sharp critique of the GOP's midterm election messaging, Jen Psaki highlighted the hypocrisy of Republicans promoting a 'common sense' candidate while running a controversial figure in Brandon Herrera. item.description: Google has announced plans to modify its search results in Europe to comply with the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA), a move aimed at avoiding potential fines. The company will prioritize comparison services like Expedia and Hotels.com while removing real-time features from hotel, airline, and restaurant results. This change, according to Google's senior vice-president Nick Fox, will 'degrade the user experience' by favoring online intermediaries over local businesses. item.title: Rare 1937 Cord 812 Supercharged Phaeton Captured in Stunning Art Deco Photos
item.description: The 1937 Cord 812 Supercharged Phaeton, designed by Gordon Buehrig, stands as one of the most innovative American automobiles of the prewar era. This Art Deco masterpiece featured groundbreaking elements such as front-wheel drive, hidden headlights, and its distinctive 'coffin-nose' styling. The supercharged variant, powered by a Lycoming V8 engine with a Schwitzer-Cummins supercharger, produced approximately 170–190 horsepower and was identifiable by its dramatic external exhaust pipes. With its low, sleek profile and advanced engineering, the 812 Phaeton remains a rare and highly prized symbol of 1930s automotive design. Vintage Everyday's collection of stunning photographs highlights the bold design and timeless sophistication of this iconic vehicle, capturing its enduring legacy as an Art Deco classic. The article emphasizes the car's historical significance, technical innovations, and its status as a cultural artifact of the 1930s automotive landscape.

item.description: This article explores the history of horse-drawn combine harvesters during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, highlighting their peak in scale and complexity as agricultural machinery. These wooden machines, powered entirely by teams of horses, transformed vast wheat fields in regions like California, Oregon, and Washington State. Farmers used massive teams of 20-40 animals, with the 33-horse hitch becoming a standard configuration. The 'skinner' driver managed the herd using specialized commands, while support staff maintained the equipment and cared for the animals. Technological advancements, such as Holt Manufacturing's link belting system, improved safety and efficiency. By the 1920s, internal combustion tractors replaced animal power, marking the end of an era. item.description: Jared Kushner, the U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law, faced sharp criticism from national security expert Alex Plitsas for his 'win-win' proposal regarding Ukraine and Russia during a recent diplomatic visit. The plan, which suggested Russia could achieve a victory without infringing on Ukrainian sovereignty, was deemed 'absolutely abhorrent' by Plitsas, who called it a disgrace to U.S. interests. The visit, part of Trump's envoy efforts with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, marked the first trip to Kyiv since the war began, but no major breakthroughs were announced. Plitsas condemned Putin's actions, citing 'documented heinous war crimes' and the deaths of hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians, emphasizing that territorial swaps should not justify Russia's aggression. item.title: Doña Ana County to Host Fall Spay/Neuter and Vaccination Clinics Through November
item.description: Doña Ana County Animal Control has announced the schedule for spay/neuter and vaccination clinics across the county from September through November 2026. Vaccination clinics will operate from 8 a.m. to 11:45 a.m. on specified dates, while spay/neuter services require appointments between 7:30 a.m. and 2 p.m. Appointments will open seven days before each clinic and must be scheduled online. Pet owners are instructed to bring dogs on leashes and cats in carriers, with pets needing to be at least three months old and in good health to receive vaccinations. Specific clinics include Holman (September 12), Salem (October 24), and Radium Springs (November 14), each with designated locations and appointment-only schedules. Walk-up services for spay/neuter will not be available, emphasizing the need for advance planning. The clinics aim to promote animal welfare while providing accessible veterinary care to residents.

item.description: Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo has accused California of driving up gas prices in his state by implementing stringent environmental regulations that reduce fuel supply. Lombardo argues that California's efforts to cut carbon emissions have led to higher fuel costs, with a gallon of gas in Nevada currently costing nearly $5, one of the highest prices in the nation. The governor claims that California's policies, such as shutting down refineries and imposing strict regulations, have significant economic impacts on neighboring states like Nevada. This narrative allows Lombardo to address voters' economic concerns without directly blaming President Donald Trump or his own party. However, Democrats argue that the surge in gas prices is primarily linked to global events like the war in Ukraine and inflationary pressures. The debate highlights the complex interplay between state policies and regional economic challenges, with Lombardo positioning himself as a critic of both California's environ

item.title: Canada to Limit Electricity Supplies to Trump Amid Trade Tensions
item.description: Canada's Energy Minister Tim Hodgson has expressed satisfaction with the prospect of withholding electricity supplies to U.S. President Donald Trump, stating that the nation's focus will remain on developing its own resources rather than exporting energy. The remarks come as Canada continues to expand its energy infrastructure, including the North Coast Transmission Line project in British Columbia, which aims to double electricity capacity to support mining and liquefied natural gas exports. Despite Trump's public criticism of Canada's energy contributions, the U.S. remains heavily reliant on Canadian electricity imports, with over 80% of its electricity imports coming from Canada in 2025. Hodgson emphasized that Canada's priorities lie in domestic development, rejecting offers to share resources with the U.S. amid ongoing trade tensions. item.title: Trump administration alters Confederate memorial description amid historical debate
item.description: The Trump administration has removed critical language from a Confederate memorial at Arlington National Cemetery, sparking controversy among historians and civil rights advocates. According to a Washington Post article, the changes involve erasing references to slavery and the Confederacy from the memorial's website and signage. The Confederate Memorial, a 32-foot bronze statue commissioned by the United Daughters of the Confederacy in 1914, was removed from the cemetery in 2023 after Congress mandated the removal of Confederate symbols from U.S. military property. The statue was relocated to the Virginia Military Institute, where it will be restored and potentially returned to Arlington in 2027. Historians like Stephen West and retired Army general Ty Seidule criticized the decision, arguing that the sanitized portrayal of the Confederacy and slavery undermines historical accuracy. Seidule called the statue 'the cruelest monument' he has ever seen, while West expressed concern over t

item.title: Legal Expert Condemns Trump's DHS Chief for On-Camera Crime, Calls for Return to Plumbing School
item.description: Legal analyst Michael Popok accused Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin of committing a federal crime by suggesting federal agents could be deployed at polling places. In a Monday episode of his 'Legal AF' podcast, Popok cited 18 U.S. Code sections 592 and 593, which prohibit armed federal officers from being present at election sites. Mullin's comments, which suggested agents could be sent to serve warrants at polling places, were deemed illegal under the statutes. Popok warned that Mullin's actions could result in five years in prison and impeachment if repeated. The legal expert also mocked Mullin's background as a plumber and homebuilder, calling the Trump administration 'comprised of dingbats and idiots.' The incident highlights tensions over election security and the legal boundaries of federal law enforcement actions.

item.description: The U.S. Federal Reserve is closely monitoring inflationary pressures and economic indicators as it prepares for critical data releases and corporate earnings reports. Central bankers are assessing the impact of recent monetary policy decisions on inflation, employment, and consumer spending. Key economic data points include the Consumer Price Index (CPI), producer price index (PPI), and employment figures, which will provide insights into the effectiveness of interest rate adjustments. Meanwhile, major corporations across technology, consumer goods, and energy sectors are set to report quarterly earnings, offering further clues about corporate performance and market sentiment. Analysts note that these reports could influence the Fed's future policy decisions, particularly regarding potential rate cuts or additional tightening measures. item.title: Elizabeth Holmes Documentary Explores Her Fall from Grace
item.description: The documentary 'You Can See Everything' provides unprecedented behind-the-scenes access to Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced founder of Theranos, as she navigates her final weeks before prison sentencing. Unveiled at the Telluride Film Festival, the film follows Nathan Fielder and a documentary crew through Holmes' 'three-year journey into the abyss,' capturing her emotional and psychological unraveling. The project, which premiered on September 7, 2026, offers a raw and unfiltered look at the aftermath of her fraud convictions, including her interactions with legal teams, media scrutiny, and personal struggles. The film's title, 'You Can See Everything,' symbolizes the intimate portrayal of her downfall, blending elements of confession, regret, and the collapse of her public persona. Critics have praised the documentary for its unflinching approach, though some argue it prioritizes spectacle over nuanced analysis. item.title: James Carville mocks Mike Johnson's claim about Congress's productivity
item.description: Political strategist James Carville turned House Speaker Mike Johnson's boast about Congress's productivity into a punchline during a segment on 'Politics War Room.' Carville and co-host Al Hunt criticized Johnson's assertion that the current Congress was the most productive since Harry Truman's in 1948, highlighting historical inaccuracies. Carville pointed out the lack of significant legislative achievements, noting that the only major bill passed was the controversial 'Big Beautiful Bill,' which many Republicans avoid campaigning on. He challenged Johnson to continue discussing the Congress's performance, comparing it to President Trump's low approval rating. Carville expressed pity for Johnson, stating he is over his head and has been manipulated by his party. The segment reflects ongoing tensions in the political landscape ahead of the 2026 midterms.

item.title: GOP Offers Free Tickets for Trump-a-Palooza Convention but Attendance Uncertain
item.description: Republican organizers are distributing free tickets to the GOP's first-ever midterm convention in Dallas, Texas, to avoid empty seats for President Donald Trump's event, known as 'Trump-a-Palooza.' However, the initiative has raised concerns as free tickets do not guarantee entry if the venue reaches capacity. The convention, which faced criticism from some lawmakers, is being promoted with a lottery system for free tickets, while others paid thousands for honorary delegate packages. Tim Bates, a GOP precinct chair, declined to pay $5,000 for a ticket, highlighting the financial barrier for many Republicans. Despite potential attendance issues, organizers project a crowd of over 20,000. The event has drawn scrutiny for its logistical challenges and the political tensions surrounding Trump's involvement. item.title: Republican candidate with fraud convictions faces allegations of exploiting ex-wives in congressional race
item.description: Jeff Belle, a Republican candidate running for Congress in San Diego, faces multiple allegations of fraud and financial exploitation of ex-wives. According to a report by the San Diego Union-Tribune, Belle has been convicted of check fraud, charged with lying on election paperwork, and fined for practicing respiratory therapy without a California license. Five former wives claim he exploited them financially, including running up credit-card debt in their names and steering one into nearly $200,000 in risky financing that led to her clinic's bankruptcy. The Union-Tribune could not verify Belle's claims of working as a U.S. Senate staffer, federal lobbyist, or private-equity CEO. Belle denied the allegations, comparing himself to Donald Trump and dismissing accusers as 'jealous.' He has also failed to file required financial disclosures for congressional candidates. His opponent, Rep. Juan Vargas, has consistently won elections with over 65% of the vote since 2012.

item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Greenland to announce a €200 million investment plan aimed at strengthening economic ties with Denmark and supporting Greenland's development in critical minerals, satellite communications, and renewable energy. The visit highlights the growing geopolitical significance of the Arctic region as melting ice opens new shipping routes and access to mineral resources. Trump's persistent demands for U.S. control over Greenland have strained transatlantic relations, prompting EU leaders to reaffirm their support for Denmark's sovereignty. Von der Leyen emphasized that Greenland's future should be decided by its people and Denmark, not external powers. The EU's expanded funding package, which includes doubling financial support to €530 million for 2028-2034, underscores the strategic importance of the Arctic in global geopolitics. item.title: Victorian Bazaars of 1880: Rare Photographs Reveal Historic Marketplaces
item.description: A collection of rare photographs from around 1880 captures the intricate designs and vibrant scenes of Victorian-era bazaars, showcasing locations such as Constantinople, Egypt, Greece, India, Normandy, Old England, Rome, Switzerland, Venice, and Scotland. The images, attributed to artist and decorator George Matthew Bridges (1854-1929) of Kings Lynn, document both the conceptual sketches and finished structures of these elaborate marketplaces. Bridges, who designed scenic bazaars, may have created the album himself to showcase his work to clients. The photographs highlight architectural details, cultural motifs, and the bustling atmosphere of these 19th-century commercial spaces. Notable entries include the 'Fairyland' bazaar backdrop, the 'Arctic' (which lacks a finished structure photo), and a draft design for a Korean bazaar. item.title: Hikers Rescued After Relying on Google Gemini for Expedition Planning
item.description: Three hikers were rescued from California’s Mount Shasta after using Google’s AI chatbot Gemini to plan their expedition, according to the Chicago Tribune. The incident highlights concerns about over-reliance on AI tools for outdoor activities. The hikers, who set off at 3am and reached the summit by 7pm despite warnings to turn back by noon, faced dangerous conditions during their descent. They called the sheriff’s office for directions and spent the night in Mud Creek Canyon before being rescued by Forest Service rangers. The sheriff’s office noted that Gemini advised the group to bring insufficient food and water, contributing to their ordeal. Authorities emphasized the importance of consulting local ranger stations and not relying solely on AI for trip planning. This case underscores the risks of using AI without proper human oversight in high-risk environments like mountain hiking. item.description: A legal scholar has warned that the U.S. Supreme Court's increasing reliance on procedural dismissals is enabling President Donald Trump to evade accountability for alleged constitutional violations. Erwin Chemerinsky, dean of the University of California, Berkeley School of Law, criticized the court's conservative majority for dismissing lawsuits against Trump on technical grounds, effectively blocking challenges to his actions. Chemerinsky highlighted recent rulings, including a 5-4 decision dismissing a case over Trump's $600 million ballroom project in the White House East Wing, arguing that the court's approach allows illegal actions to persist without judicial oversight. He emphasized that procedural rulings receive less public attention than substantive decisions, making it easier for the court to avoid scrutiny. item.title: NB Power Faces $50M Cost Due to Unplanned Outage at Point Lepreau Nuclear Plant
item.description: The Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station in New Brunswick has experienced another unplanned outage, with repair costs estimated at around $50 million. This follows a planned maintenance shutdown that was extended due to a failed gasket on the turbine system, forcing the plant offline. NB Power officials stated the outage could last until late September, potentially costing customers an additional $54 million. The utility emphasized safety in repairs and noted the incident is part of ongoing efforts to maintain reliability amid aging infrastructure. Previous outages have led to significant financial impacts, with a 2023 incident causing over $200 million in costs. The plant's low capacity factor compared to industry standards highlights operational challenges. NB Power has partnered with Ontario experts to address these issues, but rising electricity rates and growing debt continue to strain the utility. item.title: Trump's Past Juneteenth Comments Resurface During Labor Day Remarks
item.description: President Donald Trump's 2025 criticism of Juneteenth, a federal holiday commemorating the emancipation of enslaved Black Americans, resurfaced during the White House's Labor Day statement in 2026. The White House issued a message praising American workers and the Trump administration's support for them, but the post was met with backlash, including a screenshot of Trump's original social media comment. The comment, which criticized the number of non-working holidays in the U.S. and called for workers to 'get back to work,' was highlighted by Kamala Harris's 2024 campaign team. Critics argued the statement contradicted the holiday's purpose, with some noting the economic challenges under Trump's policies. The controversy underscores the ongoing political tensions surrounding labor issues and historical commemorations in the U.S.

The $LAPTOP coin's creators, including Biden, will hold 30% of the supply, with a clause to destroy up to 30% of tokens if certain conditions are met, such as a Democratic presidential victory in 2028 or Bitcoin hitting a new all-time high. item.title: Fact-checkers debunk Trump's 9/11 heroism claims as baseless
item.description: President Donald Trump's claims about his role in the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks were recently scrutinized by progressive commentator David Pakman, who called the narrative a persistent lie. In an interview with Fox News host Trey Gowdy, Trump asserted that he rushed to Ground Zero the day after the attacks and deployed construction workers to aid recovery efforts. However, Pakman's fact-checking revealed no evidence to support these claims, noting that Trump's account lacks documented proof. The commentator highlighted that Trump's own statements, such as claiming his 40 Wall Street property became the tallest building in Manhattan post-9/11, were factually incorrect. New York Fire Department officials also disputed any involvement from Trump's construction teams. Pakman emphasized that the absence of verifiable records undermines Trump's heroism narrative, which has been a recurring theme in his public statements. item.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's Labor Day Gas Price Prediction Fails
item.description: In July 2026, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, a member of President Donald Trump's Cabinet, confidently predicted that gas prices in the United States would drop to around $3 per gallon by Labor Day. However, by September 7, 2026, the national average gas price had risen to $4.15 per gallon, far exceeding Bessent's forecast. During a 'fireside chat' in Asheville, North Carolina, Bessent assured Americans that inflation, largely driven by gasoline prices, would return to $3.50 in many states and reach $3 by Labor Day. When pressed by a CBS News reporter for a specific date, Bessent replied, 'Maybe by Labor Day.' MS NOW host Peter Alexander later mocked the prediction, noting that gas prices had not only failed to meet Bessent's forecast but had instead surged to a record high for Labor Day. item.title: Milo Yiannopoulos files legal action against Laura Loomer over deportation claims
item.description: Milo Yiannopoulos, a British far-right political commentator deported by U.S. immigration authorities, has reportedly retained legal counsel to challenge Laura Loomer's claims that she facilitated his deportation. The legal notice sent to Loomer, a conspiracy theorist known for baseless allegations about Haitian immigrants and 9/11, demands she preserve all communications related to his immigration status. Yiannopoulos, who previously faced backlash for anti-Semitic remarks and racist comments about Black people, was detained and deported by ICE in August 2026. Loomer asserted she reported him to immigration authorities, but Yiannopoulos now claims he is pursuing legal action to counter her allegations. The dispute highlights ongoing tensions between online figures and immigration enforcement, with Yiannopoulos leveraging his legal team to challenge claims he deems unfounded. item.title: Trump Threatens Trade Sanctions Against Canadian Airplane Manufacturer
item.description: President Donald Trump escalated his trade conflict with Canada by targeting Bombardier, a Canadian airplane manufacturer, on Truth Social. In a fiery statement, Trump claimed the company would be banned from selling its products in the United States, accusing it of relying too heavily on American markets while blocking U.S. businesses in Canada. He accused Canada of unfairly restricting American companies like Gulfstream Aerospace and declared, 'That Era is OVER!' Trump also issued vague demands for Canadian companies to 'Buy American' and 'Fly on American Airliners.' This marks the latest in a series of trade disputes between the U.S. and Canada, with Reuters noting that Trump previously threatened import tariffs on Canadian aircraft in 2026. However, those threats yielded no results. The incident highlights ongoing tensions in U.S.-Canada trade relations and Trump's aggressive rhetoric toward foreign entities, despite the lack of concrete action from his administration.

item.title: South Park's Emmy win sparks MAGA backlash over Trump satire
item.description: The animated series 'South Park' sparked outrage among MAGA supporters after winning an Emmy with a satirical take on former President Donald Trump. The show's congratulatory message, posted on X, featured a graphic of Trump thrusting an Emmy into the air with the caption, 'You finally got your Emmy.' This is believed to reference Trump's past poor performance at the Emmys as a host of 'The Apprentice.' The latest episode also included a deep-faked, naked Trump wandering through the desert with the slogan, 'Trump: His penis is teeny-tiny, but his love for us is large.' MAGA critics expressed frustration that the show's satirical content received Emmy recognition, arguing that Trump's political influence helped secure the award. The controversy highlights ongoing tensions between conservative supporters of Trump and the entertainment industry's portrayal of political figures.

item.title: Dark Energy and Dark Matter May Share a Common Dimension
item.description: Recent astronomical observations suggest that dark energy, which drives cosmic expansion, may be weakening over time. Scientists are exploring the possibility that dark energy and dark matter are interconnected through a hypothetical 'dark dimension,' a concept rooted in string theory. This idea challenges traditional views of these mysterious components as separate entities. Researchers propose that interactions between dark energy and dark matter could explain anomalies like the Hubble tension, which highlights discrepancies in measurements of the universe's expansion rate. Theories involving a dark dimension suggest that gravitational effects from this hidden space might influence observable phenomena, offering new avenues to test cosmic theories. While these ideas remain speculative, they represent an evolving effort to unify our understanding of the cosmos' fundamental forces.

item.title: NASA Confirms Harmless Asteroid Impact Near Australia, No Threat to Humans
item.description: On September 6, a small asteroid named CERNQ52 narrowly missed Earth, passing over the Indian Ocean near northwest Australia. While initial reports suggested a potential impact, scientific analysis confirmed it posed no danger. The object, less than one meter in diameter, burned up upon entering Earth's atmosphere, creating a bright fireball visible only to those in specific locations. NASA and the European Space Agency (ESA) monitored the event, emphasizing that such small asteroids are common and typically harmless. ESA’s planetary defense experts noted the asteroid’s trajectory was well away from populated areas, and its high velocity caused it to disintegrate before reaching the surface. This incident highlights the effectiveness of global asteroid detection systems, which track near-Earth objects to ensure early warning. item.title: Ex-GOP Lawmaker Accuses Trump of Intentional 'Bizarre' AI-Slop Drop to Undermine Midterms
item.description: Former GOP House member Charlie Dent criticized President Donald Trump for his recent 'bizarre' AI-related social media posts, accusing him of intentionally undermining his party's prospects in the upcoming midterms. Dent expressed frustration over Trump's focus on trivial matters like renaming states and landmarks, arguing that this obsession with irrelevant topics distracts from critical issues such as war resolution, affordability, and national security. The ex-representative suggested that Trump's actions are not accidental but part of a deliberate strategy to harm his party's chances in the elections. Dent emphasized that while Trump's antics may appear chaotic, they could be calculated moves to weaken Republican support among voters. This critique comes amid growing concerns about the president's public behavior and its potential impact on political dynamics during a pivotal electoral period.

item.title: Photographer Shares Unpublished Photos of 9/11 Bystanders Capturing Raw Moments
item.description: A photographer named storiestellr has gained significant attention for sharing a series of unpublished, chronological photographs documenting the experiences of everyday people in New York City on September 11, 2001. The images focus on the faces of bystanders, witnesses, and ordinary citizens rather than the burning buildings, capturing their immediate reactions of confusion, disbelief, and shock as the terrorist attack unfolded. These archival photos blend a surreal mix of normalcy and growing realization, showing how individuals instinctively tried to preserve history in real time. Each image is accompanied by written captions reflecting on specific locations and moments, detailing the human experience behind the lens. The photographer explains that they intentionally turned their camera away from the World Trade Center toward the crowd, posting these photos daily from September 11, 2021, until September 11, 2026, to chronicle the emotional impact of the event over two decades. item.description: President Donald Trump delivered a highly polarizing Labor Day message that focused on attacking political opponents rather than celebrating workers. In a social media post, Trump labeled left-wing activists as 'Radical Left Lunatics, Communists, and Dumocrats' who seek to destroy the United States. item.description: The article discusses an ongoing investigation into allegations that former President Donald Trump may have used a spy phone to conduct illicit communications. The claims emerged amid heightened scrutiny of his administration's activities, with sources suggesting the device was used to intercept sensitive information. Trump's legal team has denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated and part of a broader effort to undermine his presidency. The controversy has reignited debates about executive privilege, national security protocols, and the ethical boundaries of political power. The piece also highlights historical precedents of similar investigations, emphasizing the tension between transparency and confidentiality in high-level governance. item.title: David Bowie's Sphinx Series: Capturing His Transformation into a Global Superstar
item.description: The Sphinx Series, often referred to as the 'Hunky Dory Sphinx' sessions, represents a pivotal moment in David Bowie's career, marking his transition from a folk-rock singer to a global superstar. Photographed by Brian Ward in 1971 at his London studio on Heddon Street, these images captured Bowie in a state of high-fashion androgyny that would define the Hunky Dory era. During this period, Bowie was deeply engaged in recording his album Hunky Dory, experimenting with his image to move away from his late 1960s 'curly-haired mod' look toward a more ethereal, gender-fluid aesthetic. The series features Bowie with long, flowing strawberry-blonde hair, wearing a floral 'man-dress' designed by Michael Fish, which he also wore on the cover of The Man Who Sold the World. The name 'Sphinx Series' originates from Bowie's rigid, symmetrical posing, sitting on the floor with legs tucked and a piercing gaze directed at the camera. item.title: Global Defense Spending Surge Drives Growth in Military Contractors
item.description: The article discusses the surge in global defense spending and its impact on military contractors. In 2025, defense companies recorded record revenues, with the top firms like Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman leading the growth. The U.S. and European nations increased defense budgets significantly, driven by geopolitical tensions such as Russia's invasion of Ukraine. This has led to production bottlenecks and a shift in business strategies toward European-made equipment. Companies are expanding into various domains including air defense, naval shipbuilding, and cyber warfare. The article highlights the economic effects, noting job creation in defense sectors and the transformation of industries like automotive and rail into drone manufacturing. item.title: Study Links High Coffee Consumption to Lower Bone Density in Postmenopausal Women
item.description: A study conducted by Flinders University and published in the journal Nutrients found that high coffee consumption may be associated with lower bone mineral density (BMD) in older, postmenopausal women. Researchers analyzed data from 9,704 women aged 65 and older over a 10-year period, measuring BMD at key fracture-prone sites like the femoral neck and hip. The findings revealed that tea consumption was linked to higher total hip BMD, while drinking more than five cups of coffee daily correlated with reduced BMD. Moderate coffee intake (2-3 cups/day) showed no negative effects on bone health. However, factors like alcohol intake and obesity influenced these associations, with tea's positive impact being more pronounced in obese women. The study highlights the potential role of dietary habits in bone health but emphasizes that observational data cannot prove causation. item.title: Expert links 'mystery meat' risks to Melania Trump's connections and international food safety concerns
item.description: A new analysis warns of potential health risks from 'mystery meat' imported into the U.S., linking the issue to Melania Trump's connections and questionable food safety practices abroad. Author Eric Schlosser of 'Fast Food Nation' highlights the dangers of inexpensive, potentially contaminated meat sourced from countries like Uruguay, Argentina, and Brazil. These nations have faced scandals involving banned antibiotics and anti-parasitic drugs in their beef exports. Schlosser argues that the U.S. decision to import 300,000 metric tons of ground beef without tariffs could benefit meatpacking companies and fast food chains at the expense of American ranchers and consumers. He urges people to buy fresh, locally sourced beef instead of mass-produced processed meat. item.description: The article discusses Tesla's recent Cybercab event in Austin, highlighting concerns over the company's autonomous vehicle rollout. Despite CEO Elon Musk's absence from the event, which lacked the usual fanfare, the focus remains on Tesla's ability to launch a safe and scalable robotaxi service. item.description: A senior aide to Senator Mike Rounds (R-SD) has been secretly lobbying for major corporations while serving as a Senate staffer, according to newly released South Dakota state filings. item.title: Indonesia's Peat Fires Pose Severe Environmental Threats Amid El Niño
item.description: The article details the escalating crisis of underground peat fires in Indonesia, exacerbated by El Niño conditions. These fires, which burn beneath the surface, release massive amounts of carbon dioxide and other pollutants, contributing to global climate change. Unlike surface fires, they are harder to detect and extinguish, posing significant challenges for firefighting efforts. The piece highlights how these fires have become a recurring problem, particularly in regions like Kalimantan and Sumatra, where peatlands are extensive. Scientists warn that the fires not only destroy ecosystems but also release ancient carbon stored for centuries, worsening atmospheric pollution. item.title: The Antarctic Sun Starfish: A Master of Deep-Sea Adaptation
item.description: The Antarctic sun starfish (Labidiaster annulatus), also known as the wolftrap starfish, is a remarkable deep-sea predator with up to 50 flexible arms resembling octopus tentacles. These arms are lined with microscopic jaw-like pincers called pedicellariae, which function like bear traps to capture prey. Thriving in freezing Antarctic waters as low as -2°C, this species dominates one of the harshest environments on Earth. Its ability to survive up to an hour in icy conditions and use razor-sharp teeth to scrape ice highlights its evolutionary adaptations. The Antarctic sun starfish is an opportunistic hunter, feeding on krill, amphipods, small fish, and even other sea stars. Scientists describe it as a 'Death Star' due to its formidable appearance and hunting prowess. Despite its intimidating features, the species plays a crucial role in the Southern Ocean ecosystem, showcasing nature's resilience in extreme climates.

item.title: Serbia honors war crimes suspect with military funeral amid EU backlash
item.description: Ratko Mladić, the Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide and war crimes during the 1992-95 Bosnian War, received a full military funeral in Serbia despite European Union condemnation. The funeral, held at Belgrade's Church of St. Luke, drew thousands of mourners who viewed Mladić as a hero. Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic defended the ceremony, calling it an emotional outpouring unrelated to his past policies. The EU criticized Serbia for glorifying a war criminal, with enlargement commissioner Marta Kos canceling a planned visit to protest the honors. Mladić, who died in prison at 84, was sentenced in 2017 for orchestrating the Srebrenica massacre and other atrocities. His burial followed similar treatment of another convicted war criminal, Nebojsa Pavkovic, highlighting Serbia's resistance to acknowledging its wartime role. The country's EU accession bid faces delays due to political tensions and refusal to join sanctions against Russia.

item.title: Researchers Identify Dormant Breast Cancer Cells Protected by Immune Barriers
item.description: A groundbreaking study reveals that breast cancer cells can remain dormant for years by hiding behind protective barriers formed by immune cells. Researchers from the Medical Research Council (MRC) Laboratory of Medical Sciences discovered that these cancer cells evade detection by creating a shield-like environment, which allows them to persist undetected in the body. The study, published in *Genome Medicine*, highlights how these dormant cells co-evolve with their surroundings, forming niches that support their survival. This discovery has significant implications for cancer treatment, as it explains why some tumors recur even after prolonged remission. The research team used advanced spatial analysis techniques to map the interactions between proliferative and dormant cancer cells, revealing a dynamic ecosystem within tumors. Research comparing exchange-based pricing to conventional bookmakers found liquidity plays a critical role in trade execution, with busy markets offering better price matching opportunities.
